title: Phalar Aluve
html:
Phalar Aluve is a rare +1 Longsword that can be made to  Sing or  Shriek, granting nearby allies or enemies a bonus to Attack Rolls or damage rolls, depending on the choice.

The Drow inscription on this blade appears to have been recently carved. It translates to;
“
'Though I have to leave you, I will dance forever in Eilistraee's Light.'
 „

Special

The holder of this item gains:

  •  Performance +1
 Phalar Aluve: Melody ()
The sword hums in anticipation, ready to  Sing or  Shriek (see bugs on their respective pages). ( Recharge: Short rest.)

Weapon actions

If you have proficiency, equip in main hand to gain:

 Lacerate ()
Slash at your target's vital points to make it  Bleed. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
 Pommel Strike ()
Make a non-lethal attack against an enemy and possibly  Daze them. ( Recharge: Short rest.)
 Rush Attack ()
Charge forward and attack the first enemy in your way, possibly pushing them  Off Balance. ( Recharge: Short rest.)

Where to find

  • Underdark X: 116 Y: -192: Embedded inside a rock

Notes

  • The sword can be freed in these ways:
    • Passing a  DC 15 Strength Check to yank it from the stone.
    • Passing a  DC 15 Religion Check to learn how to release the magic holding it in place. Clerics of Lolth have advantage on this check.
    • Paladins can pass a  DC 10 Religion Check (with  Advantage) to consider what the appropriate ritual for releasing the sword is. If successful, they can perform the ritual or use their oath to prove their worth ( DC 10 Charisma Check).
    • Clerics of  Eilistraee can release the sword without needing an ability check.
    • Spilling blood on the sword outside dialogue also releases it. It is possible to make one party member hit another, or perform a  Blood Sacrifice if a party member has the  Ritual Dagger, to cover the sword in a  Blood surface. It is also possible throw a dead body on the sword. This will make it light up, so it can be pulled out without any ability check.
  • Longswords do not normally have the  Finesse property; Phalar Aluve is special in this regard. The only other example is  Larethian's Wrath.
  • Phalar Aluve is Drow language. Phalar means 'battle-marker' or 'grave', and Aluve means 'I/we leave you'.
  • Obtaining the sword grants the inspiration ⁠Last Rites of the Dark Dancer for party members with the  Acolyte background, unless the sword was obtained through the dialogue option of a paladin using the strength of their oath.
  • Although it has a distinctive appearance during the cutscene for its retrieval, when equipped this sword has an appearance similar to that of a  Longsword +1, save for its blade, hilt and pommel, which are gold instead of polished steel.
